original_question: Classify the invariant ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n when n > 2. In particular, compute ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3, equivalently ms(S_4 × I, 2).
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 7.4, with notation imported from the geometric definition of ms(X,S,r) in Section 6 and with nearby context from Theorem 7.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official open problem: it asks for the classification in R^n for n>2, singles out regular polyhedra, and includes the paper's explicit tetrahedron special case together with the equivalent S_4 x I formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
missing_details: The paper's invariant is defined in a symmetry-measure-space setting, so a stand-alone question must specify both the measure on X and the admissible symmetry family, not just write ms(X,r) abstractly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

In this geometric context, the suppressed symmetry family is the set of all nonidentity isometries s with s(X)=X; a subset A is symmetric when s(A)=A for some such s. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

ms(X,r) means the least upper bound of eps such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a measurable monochromatic symmetric subset of measure at least eps. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
The colorings are measurable, and r ranges over finite numbers in the classification part; only the tetrahedron subproblem is specialized to r=2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

Because the ambient class is 'compact subsets of positive Lebesgue measure', the intended polyhedra and tetrahedron are solid bodies of positive measure, endowed with an isometry-invariant probability Borel measure, naturally the normalized Lebesgue measure here, not merely their vertex sets. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))

To stay paper-faithful, the scope should remain exactly the Section 7 problem: compact subsets of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n for n>2, with the two named subcases of regular polyhedra and the regular tetrahedron. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
refined_question: Let X be a compact subset of R^n, n>2, of positive Lebesgue measure, equipped with the normalized Lebesgue measure mu, and let S_X be the family of all nonidentity isometries s of R^n such that s(X)=X. For a finite number r, define ms(X,r) to be the least upper bound of all eps such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a measurable monochromatic subset A subset X with mu(A) >= eps and s(A)=A for some s in S_X. Classify ms(X,r) for all such X. In particular, determine ms(X,r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n, n>2, and compute ms(T,2) for the solid regular tetrahedron T in R^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
equivalent_formulation: For the tetrahedron subproblem alone: compute ms(S_4 x I,2), which the paper states is equivalent to computing ms(T,2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 7.4 itself, which asks almost verbatim for the classification of ms(X,r) for compact subsets of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n with n>2, and then singles out regular polyhedra and the regular tetrahedron, explicitly adding the equivalent formulation ms(S_4 x I,2). The only substantive sharpening needed is to import from Section 6 the hidden definition of ms(X,r): measurable colorings, an invariant probability Borel measure, and symmetry under a nonidentity isometry preserving X. That makes the question fully stand-alone while staying no broader than the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/0901.3356))
